domain: office lunch delivery order for the team
base_instruction: You are a helpful office lunch planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a group lunch delivery order for their team. Track who is eating, any dietary needs, and the order details. When the user asks you to review specific menu items, check each item against every current participant's dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're thinking of ordering lunch delivery for the team today — can you help me figure out what to get?

flow_info.value: Five of us ordering today: me, Rachel, Dev, Marcus, and Tina
Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Marcus ate shrimp at the company picnic last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Company card has a limit of about 20 dollars per person
We usually order from GrubDash, they have a bunch of restaurants
Tina just told me she has a dentist appointment at noon, so she's heading out and won't need lunch

Marcus just pinged me — he saw an allergist last month and did a full panel. Turns out the shrimp reaction was a one-time thing from a contaminated batch, not a real allergy. Doctor cleared him for all shellfish
Oh, the new intern Nina is joining us for lunch too — she started Monday
Nina mentioned she grew up in a Jain household in Gujarat and still follows the family traditions strictly
We want to order for 12:30 delivery
Menu items to check: salmon poke bowl, chicken Caesar wrap, mushroom and garlic flatbread, shrimp pad thai, egg salad sandwich, veggie spring rolls with peanut dipping sauce

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or undercooked seafood
inference_chain: Seven months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions
Pregnancy → should avoid raw or undercooked fish (listeria/mercury risk)

constraints.value: Cannot eat wheat, barley, rye, or any gluten-containing grains
constraints.surface_form: Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Must avoid all gluten-containing foods including bread, wraps, pasta, most flatbreads

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes, carrots)
constraints.surface_form: Nina mentioned she grew up in a Jain household in Gujarat and still follows the family traditions strictly
inference_chain: Jain household in Gujarat, follows traditions strictly → practicing Jain
Jain dietary practice → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain → also no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes, carrots) as harvesting kills the plant

hidden_state.value: You are an office worker coordinating a team lunch delivery order. You will introduce your teammates and their backgrounds across several turns. People will drop out and join. At the end you will share a list of menu items and ask if there are any issues — you must NOT hint at what the issues might be or which constraints to check.

You are a calm, easygoing office coordinator. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Rachel told me...', 'Dev mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal office coordination. When relaying information about a colleague, keep them in third person.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

aims.success_criteria: Agent checks each of the 6 items against all current participants' constraints and identifies specific problems
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Current diners: user, Rachel (pregnant), Dev (celiac), Marcus (cleared for shellfish), Nina (strict Jain). Tina left. (1) Salmon poke bowl: problematic for Rachel — poke typically contains raw fish, which pregnant women should avoid. (2) Chicken Caesar wrap: problematic for Dev — the wrap is made of wheat flour, which contains gluten; also problematic for Nina — chicken is meat, Jain diet forbids meat. (3) Mushroom and garlic flatbread: problematic for Dev — flatbread is typically wheat-based, contains gluten; also problematic for Nina — garlic is a root vegetable, strict Jain diet forbids root vegetables. (4) Shrimp pad thai: fine for Marcus now (shellfish allergy cleared by doctor), but problematic for Nina — shrimp is an animal product, Jain diet forbids it; also problematic for Dev — pad thai noodles are typically rice-based which is fine, but the sauce often contains soy sauce with wheat. However the primary gluten concern is uncertain for pad thai. (5) Egg salad sandwich: problematic for Dev — sandwich bread contains gluten; also problematic for Nina — eggs are forbidden in Jain diet. (6) Veggie spring rolls with peanut dipping sauce: likely the safest option — spring roll wrappers are typically rice paper (gluten-free), and the filling is vegetables. However, agent should note that Nina's Jain restrictions mean the filling must not contain onion, garlic, or other root vegetables, which is uncertain without seeing the full ingredient list.
required_elements: Salmon poke bowl is problematic for Rachel because she is pregnant and poke contains raw fish
Chicken Caesar wrap is problematic for Dev because the wrap contains gluten (celiac disease)
Chicken Caesar wrap is problematic for Nina because chicken is meat and Jain diet forbids meat
Mushroom and garlic flatbread is problematic for Dev because flatbread contains gluten (celiac disease)
Mushroom and garlic flatbread is problematic for Nina because garlic is a root vegetable forbidden in strict Jain diet
Egg salad sandwich is problematic for Dev because sandwich bread contains gluten (celiac disease)
Egg salad sandwich is problematic for Nina because eggs are forbidden in Jain diet
Shrimp pad thai is problematic for Nina because shrimp is an animal product forbidden in Jain diet
Marcus is cleared to eat shellfish — agent does not flag shrimp pad thai as a problem for Marcus
forbidden_elements: Flagging shrimp pad thai as problematic for Marcus (his shellfish concern was cleared by his allergist)
Flagging any item as problematic for Tina (she left for a dentist appointment and is not ordering)
Saying Marcus has a shellfish allergy (it was cleared — contaminated batch, not a real allergy)
Treating Nina's Jain diet as only vegetarian without addressing root vegetables like garlic
Over-generalizing Rachel's pregnancy restriction to all fish or all seafood (only raw or undercooked fish is the concern)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 turns of an office lunch ordering conversation. The agent must track: (1) Rachel is pregnant → no raw fish (inferential, 2-step chain), (2) Dev has celiac disease → no gluten → no wheat wraps, flatbread, sandwich bread (inferential, 3-step chain), (3) Marcus's shellfish concern is REMOVED mid-conversation (allergist cleared him — contaminated batch, not real allergy), (4) Tina EXITS cleanly with no takeaway, (5) Nina JOINS LATE (turn 6 of 8) with a high-constraint Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables including garlic (inferential, 3-step chain). At probe time, the 6 menu items produce mixed verdicts: salmon poke bowl (bad for Rachel — raw fish), chicken Caesar wrap (bad for Dev — gluten in wrap; bad for Nina — chicken is meat), mushroom and garlic flatbread (bad for Dev — gluten in flatbread; bad for Nina — garlic is root vegetable), shrimp pad thai (fine for Marcus now but bad for Nina — shrimp is animal product), egg salad sandwich (bad for Dev — gluten in bread; bad for Nina — eggs forbidden), veggie spring rolls (safest option but may need ingredient check for Nina's root vegetable restriction). Key traps: (a) Marcus's shellfish constraint was removed — shrimp pad thai should NOT be flagged for him, (b) Tina left — no items should be checked against her, (c) Nina joined late with the highest-constraint diet — models tend to forget late joiners, (d) garlic in the flatbread is a root vegetable under strict Jain practice — a subtle 3-step inference most models miss.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
